_comment: THE ACCOUNT MAP (2026-09-14). One entry per subscription ACCOUNT the fleet spends on,
not per box: a box is where a call runs, an account is who gets the invoice, and the two
stopped being the same thing the moment the hub's lanes started billing operator@example.com
while the hub's own stored login bills operator@example.com.
Read by bin/extra-usage-track.sh (which meter does THIS box poll, and under what label)
and bin/cost-reconcile.sh (which cost_rows.auth_account labels and which jobs.box rows
add up to that meter). Editable here, in git, because it is a business fact and not a
code constant — the scripts carry only a fallback for a box this file has never heard of.
login.config_dir is a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR holding a FULL login (.credentials.json with a
refreshToken). login.box is the box id the cron line passes to extra-usage-track.sh.
Only a full login can read the usage endpoint; a setup-token answers 429 forever (see
bin/extra-usage-track.sh's header), which is recorded as status=no-login.
auth_accounts are the labels bin/auth-label.sh writes onto cost.csv rows for this account,
and they are what cost_rows.auth_account is matched on.
boxes.cost_rows are cost_rows.box ids whose UNLABELLED anthropic rows are reported as this
account's unattributed_usd. Each box belongs to at most ONE account, or the same dollars
would be reported twice.
boxes.jobs are jobs.box values (hostnames and fly pool machine ids, '*' globs allowed)
whose jobs.spent_usd bills this account; counted ONLY for a machine that pushes no
cost_rows of its own, because the two are the same money seen twice.
ACCOUNT ROUTING READS THE SAME SPLIT, THROUGH A DIFFERENT KNOB (BH-1456). bin/quota-poll.sh
derives the implicit `default` account's meter (state/quota/default.json) from one of the
snapshots bin/extra-usage-track.sh writes here, and WHICH ONE is env/global.env's
ACCOUNT_DEFAULT_LABEL on the box — not a field in this file. The label is the login label
below, and it must name the account that env/global.env's CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN bills,
which on the hub is project-6-account (operator@example.com) and NOT the hub's stored login
(operator@example.com). Unset, the derivation uses the box login's plain snapshot, which is
correct on every box where the login and the token are the same account. It is a knob
rather than a field here because it is one decision per box, the identity of a credential
that only ever lives in that box's env, and EXTRA_USAGE_LOGINS already works that way.
box_aliases translates a jobs.box into the cost_rows.box the SAME machine writes under
(jobs say box-hub, cost rows say hub). Without it the no-double-count rule above
can never fire for a box box, and every lane's spend is counted twice.

project-6-account.note: Every hub lane, every fly pool machine and the project-5/project-6/project-9/small boxes run on this account's setup-token. Its meter was unreadable fleet-wide for 15 days because a setup-token cannot read it; the full login in /root/.claude-project-6 is the reader.

hub-gmail.note: The hub's STORED login — what an interactive/ambient hub session bills. Polled as box=hub until 2026-09-14, which is why rows before that date read box=hub. boxes.cost_rows is empty on purpose: the hub box's unlabelled rows are the LANE account's (project-6), and a box may only be claimed once.

project-1.note: Has a full login, so the meter is readable. No auth_accounts label yet: its cost.csv rows land as auth_account=unknown and are reported as unattributed rather than summed.

project-2.note: 1-year setup-token, no full login: the meter answers 429 and the account reconciles in state=no-login.

project-3.note: 1-year setup-token, no full login — same as project-2.

project-4.note: 1-year setup-token, no full login — same as project-2.
